Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:1.english: Matters that a person does not ascertain - [That is, ascertain them] clearly so as to state them properly.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:2.hebrew: אלא אם כן נכשל בהן - עד שאומרן ב' וג' פעמים בשיבוש, דהיינו טעמי תורה המסותרין:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:2.english: Unless he stumbles over them - Until he states them two or three times in error; that is, the hidden reasons of the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:3.hebrew: לא אהיה חובש - איני רגיל להיות חובש, חבוש בבהמ"ד. אהיה — הורגלתי, כמו ״שחוק לרעהו אהיה״ (איוב י״ב:ד׳), אני הווה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:3.english: I will not be a ruler [chovesh] - I am not accustomed to being a chovesh — [i.e.,] confined [chavush] in the study hall. "I will be" [ehyeh] [means] I am accustomed, as in: "I am [ehyeh] a laughingstock to his friend" (Job 12:4) — [meaning] I am [habitually].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:4.hebrew: וממאי - דמשום דיש בהן אמנה הוא? דילמא על כרחיך צריכים שישיבו האמת:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:4.english: And from what - [do you conclude] that it is because they have faithfulness? Perhaps perforce they must answer the truth.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:5.english: For if he had said to them, “I have learned” - [namely,] those reasons of the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:6.english: They say to him - They ask [him], “Tell us.”

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:7.english: And [the Gemara] answers: He could have said [that] he learned and forgot; what [is meant by] "I will not be a ruler"? - He is admitting the truth, that he did not toil in Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:1:8.english: In matters of Torah - They were trustworthy and would not boast falsely.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:2:1.english: And a round [cake] of pressed figs - For it is large and there are many meals in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:2:2.english: And if they were clever - [That is,] to ask for their wages as laborers.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:1.hebrew: לחצר המעורבת - ואפי' הכי, טובא לא ליצול, כדאמר לעיל (שבת דף קיז:), מתוך שבהול, אי שרי לאיעסוקי בהצלה כולי האי, אתי לכבויי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:1.english: To a courtyard where an eiruv was established - Even so, he should not rescue a great deal, as [the Gemara] stated above (Shabbat 117b): since he is panicked, if it were permitted [for him] to occupy himself with rescuing so much, he would come to extinguish [the fire].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:2.hebrew: כל כלי תשמישו - שצריכין לו לאותו היום, כגון כוסות וקיתוניות:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:2.english: All the utensils for his use - [Those] that he needs for that day, such as cups and pitchers.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:3.hebrew: י"ח כלים - מפרש להו בגמרא, שכן דרך ללובשן בחול יחד, אבל טפי מהכי לא, ואינו פושטן לחזור וללבוש ולהציל אחרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:3:3.english: Eighteen garments - They are explained in the Gemara, for such is the way to wear them together on a weekday; but more than this, no, and he does not take them off to return and put on [other garments] and rescue others.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:1.hebrew: בבא להציל - [שהציל] בסל [אחד], כדקתני "סל מלא ככרות", ואינו טורח אלא להצילן מתוך הדליקה בבת אחת — מציל כל מה שבסל, דהא חדא זימנא הוא; מה לי פורתא, מה לי טובא:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:1.english: When one comes to rescue - [That is,] where he rescued [them] in one basket, as [the Mishnah] teaches, "a basket full of loaves," and he only exerts himself to rescue them from the fire all at once — he may rescue everything that is in the basket, for it is [only] one time; what [difference is it] to me [whether it is] a little, [and] what [difference is it] to me [whether it is] a lot?

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:2.hebrew: בבא לקפל - סלים הרבה זה עם זה, לטרוח [ולאוספם] ולחזור ולהוציא, מזון ג' סעודות הוא דיכול להציל בסלים הרבה ותו לא, שכל א' טורח בעצמו הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:2.english: When one comes to collect - many baskets together, to exert himself and gather them and go back and bring [them] out, it is [only] food for three meals that he may rescue in many baskets, and no more, for each one is an exertion in itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:3.hebrew: פירש טליתו וקיפל והניח - הביא אוכלין והניח, וחזר והביא והניח, מהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:3.english: He spread his cloak and collected and placed - He brought food and placed [it], and again brought [food] and placed [it]; what is [the ruling]?

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:4.hebrew: כבא להציל דמי - הואיל ואין כאן אלא כלי אחד, ובפעם אחת הוא מוציאם:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:4.english: Is he considered like one who comes to rescue - Since there is only one vessel here, and he takes them out all at once.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:4:5.english: Or is he like one who comes to collect - Since he takes the trouble to gather and collect.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:1.hebrew: אטעייה רב שיזבי לרב חסדא - שדרש לפניו והודה לו רב חסדא. ואהא מתני' דאמרן לעיל (שבת דף קיז:): "נשברה לו חבית בראש גגו, מביא כלי ומניח תחתיה" — ודרש רב שיזבי לרב חסדא: "ובלבד שלא יתן כלי המחזיק יותר משלש סעודות", והודה לו רב חסדא. ומדאמר רבא "אטעייה", שמע מינה טעותא הוא, דאפילו מחזיק סעודות הרבה מותר, כיון דחד מנא הוא; והאי כמקפל ונותן בכלי אחד דמי, דהא מעט מעט הוא נופל ומטפטף בו. ש"מ בחד מנא כבא להציל דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:1.english: Rav Sheizvi misled Rav Chisda - for he expounded before him and Rav Chisda agreed with him. And [this was] regarding this Mishnah that we said earlier (Shabbat 117b): "If a barrel broke for him on top of his roof, he brings a vessel and places [it] underneath it" — and Rav Sheizvi expounded to Rav Chisda: "provided that he does not place a vessel that holds more than three meals," and Rav Chisda agreed with him. And since Rava said, "He misled him," conclude from this that it is an error, for even [a vessel] that holds many meals is permitted, since it is one vessel; and this is like one who gathers [food] and places [it] in one vessel, since it falls and drips into it little by little. Conclude from this [that] with one vessel, it is like one who comes to rescue.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:2.english: What is the error - From where do you [know] that it is an error on his part?

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:3.english: He said to him - [I know this] from that which is taught in it, in the Baraita:

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:4.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יביא כלי אחר וכו' - ש"מ כלים טובא הוא דאסירי, אבל בחד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:5:4.english: Provided that he does not bring another vessel, etc. - Conclude from this [that] it is many vessels that are forbidden, but with one [vessel] it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:1.hebrew: מהפקירא וכו' - דהא הצילו לכם קאמר להו, לצרכיהם; ואם פקחים הם, יעכבו הכל — הוה ליה למיתני:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:1.english: From ownerless [property], etc. - For he says to them, "Rescue for yourselves," [meaning] for their own needs; and it should have taught: "If they are clever, they may keep everything."

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:2.english: An attribute of piety - That they return [it] to him.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:3.hebrew: חסידי אגרא דשבתא שקלי - בתמיה. אם חסידים הם, יש להם לוותר משלהם בכל דבר שיש בו נדנוד עבירה. ואע"ג דלאו שכר שבת גמור הוא — שהרי לא התנה, ומהפקירא קא זכו — מיהו חסיד לא מיקרי אא"כ מוותר משלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:3.english: Do pious people take payment for Shabbat - [This is said] in astonishment. If they are pious, they should forgo [what is] theirs in any matter in which there is [even] a trace of transgression. And even though it is not full-fledged Shabbat pay — for he did not stipulate [a wage], and they acquire [the items] from ownerless property — nevertheless, one is not called pious unless he forgoes [what is] his.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:4.hebrew: הכא בירא שמים עסקינן - המציל הזה ירא שמים הוא, ולא חסיד לוותר משלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:4.english: Here we are dealing with one who is Heaven-fearing - This rescuer is Heaven-fearing, but not pious [enough] to forgo his own.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:5.hebrew: דלא ניחא ליה דליתהני מאחריני - בזכייה דהפקירא, דידע דלא מרצונו הפקירו:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:5.english: That it is uncomfortable for him to benefit from others - [That is,] through the acquisition of ownerless [property], for he knows that [the owner] did not declare it ownerless willingly.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:6.english: And it is also not agreeable to him to exert himself for free - For he is not a pious person [so as] to forgo what is his.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:7.hebrew: והכי קאמר כו' - כלומר, דהאי "אם היו פקחין" דמתני' לאו פקחין בדין קאמר ליטול את הראוי להם, דאם כן, "יעכבו הכל" הוה ליה למתני. אלא לאו הכי קאמר: הני יראי שמים, אם פקחין הן בהלכות שבת, דידעי דכה"ג לאו שכר שבת הוא — דמעיקרא לאו אדעתא דשכר פעולה נחית — עושין עמו חשבון. ו"הכי קאמר" אדרב חסדא נמי קאי, אלא לא שבקיניה לרב חסדא לסיימיה למילתיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:6:7.english: And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying, etc. - That is to say, this [phrase] "if they were clever" of the Mishnah does not mean clever in law, to take what is fitting for them, for if so, it should have taught "they may keep everything." Rather, does it not mean this: these Heaven-fearing [people], if they are clever in the laws of Shabbat, such that they know that in a case like this it is not Shabbat payment — since originally they did not enter [into it] with the intention of [receiving] a wage for [their] labor — they make a calculation with him. And "And this is what it is saying" applies to Rav Chisda['s statement] as well, except that they did not allow Rav Chisda to finish his statement.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:10.english: Pargod - Genouillières [knee-high leggings in Old French], and in German, Kniehosen [knee-hose].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:11.english: A belt - [Worn] over his tunic, on the inside.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:12.hebrew: וסודר שבצוארו - ותלויין ראשיו לפניו, לקנח בו פיו ועיניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:12.english: And a scarf around his neck - and its ends hang down in front of him, to wipe his mouth and his eyes with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:2.hebrew: אונקלי - לבוש רחב כעין שריניש"א, ובלשון ערבי מחשיא"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:2.english: A cape [unkali] - A broad garment like a sherinisha, and in the Arabic language, machshiyah.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:3.english: Punda - A hollow belt [worn] over his garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:4.english: Kalbus - [In Old French,] navies [a type of garment].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:5.english: A robe - A chemise [shirt worn] against his skin.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:6.english: And apilyon - A sheet in which to wrap one's entire [body].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:7.english: Ma'poret [a kerchief] - [A cloth] to wrap his head.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:8:8.english: And two straps [sefarkin] - [In Old French:] feisols [straps or bands].

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:9:2.hebrew: מפני שהוא מחרך - מן האור, ובלע"ז רטריי"ט, ואינו נשרף, ומתוך כך הוא מגין על התיבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 120a:9:2.english: Because it is singed - from the fire — and in Old French, retrait [shriveled] — and it does not burn, and thereby it protects the chest.

Rashi on Shabbat 120a:9:4.english: For they cannot withstand the force of the fire - Because they are new.

Tosafot on Shabbat 120a:10:1.hebrew: נותן מים מצד זה - פירש רשב"ם: לאו דוקא על הטלית, דהא קי"ל בפ' דם חטאת (זבחים צד:) דבבגד שרייתו זהו כיבוסו; ולעיל בסוף פרק שמנה שרצים (שבת דף קיא.) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120a:10:1.english: One places water on this side - Rashbam explained: [This does] not literally [mean] on the garment [itself], for we hold as an established rule in Chapter Dam Chatat (Zevachim 94b) that with a garment, soaking it constitutes its laundering; and above, at the end of Chapter Shemonah Sheratzim (Shabbat 111a), I explained [this].

Tosafot on Shabbat 120a:4:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי בבא לקפל - פירש הרב פורת, דלקפל היינו אפי' בא לקפל, דלר' אבא אין חילוק בין לקפל בין להציל, דאפילו להציל בחצר אחרת לא שרי אלא מזון ג' סעודות. אבל אין נראה לומר דלהציל שרי אפילו מאה סעודות בחצר אחרת גם לרבי אבא, דאם כן הוה ליה לאוקומי מתני' אידי ואידי בחצר אחרת, וכאן בבא לקפל וכאן בבא להציל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 120a:4:1.english: Both this and that [refer to] one who comes to collect - Rav Porat explained that "to collect" means even one who comes to collect, for according to Rabbi Abba there is no distinction between collecting and rescuing, as even to rescue [and bring] to a different courtyard is permitted only [up to] food for three meals. However, it does not seem [correct] to say that to rescue is permitted even a hundred meals [when bringing] to a different courtyard even according to Rabbi Abba, because if so, he should have established the Mishnahs [as] both [referring] to a different courtyard, with this [one referring] to one who comes to collect and that [one] to one who comes to rescue.
